...with a snapping sound, the ofuda broke. And so did the barrier. Memories flooded back to the thing that used to be; now remembered that is used to be Yoshika Miyako. There were music and poems. The gentle rustle of leaves within the wind. A distant roar as waves hit upon a rocky shore. Calligraphy under the warm glow of a candle.

Then there was darkness. When it receded, the world was bathed in twilight, its rich colors reduced to foggy shaded of grey. Everything had been dulled down. Yoshika could no longer feel the warm rays of the sun on her skin. Sounds were muffled as if her head was underwater. Even pain, sharp and stinging, only existed as a weird, tingling sensation.

At least she could still taste things. She still knew the sweetness of cherries and the sourness of apples, the metallic flavor of blood and...the warm tenderness of still-living flesh and...the musky softness of bloated bodies, torrents of liquefied organs showering her tongue with every bite.

Yoshika Miyako trembled as every fiber of her reawakened consciousness screamed to throw up, but the responsible nerves no longer functioned. The nausea as she imaged the blacked, necrotic pieces of tissue and lumps of coagulated blood in her stomach was unbearable. She fell to her knees, her body convulsing as she desperately tried to eject the rotting flesh inside her.

When the Wicked Hermit returned soon after, Ofuda in hand and sardonic smile in her face, Yoshika did not even attempt to resist. She no longer wanted to remember.
